drivingQuestion: Are distinguishing marks valid identification by Torah law?
outcomeNote: The question opens a discussion continued in the next unit.

segments.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ סִימָנִין וְכוּ׳. לְמֵימְרָא דְּסִימָנִין לָאו דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא.
segments.en: § We learned in the mishna that, «although there are distinguishing marks» on a dead person’s body and clothing, one may not rely on these as identification. The Gemara asks: «Is this to say that distinguishing marks are not» recognized as valid identification «by Torah law,» and while a rabbinic ordinance allows one to rely upon them to remedy certain situations, for testimony about a person’s death, the Sages require the stringencies of Torah law?
